# maek

> maek is a zero-auth HTTP tunnel server. It exposes a local application
> (e.g. http://localhost:3000) at a public URL on this host - no account,
> no API key.

This server's base URL: __SERVER_URL__

## Expose a local app

1. Install the CLI:

   macOS/Linux:
     curl -fsSL __SERVER_URL__/_maek/install.sh | sh
   Windows (PowerShell):
     irm __SERVER_URL__/_maek/install.ps1 | iex
   Or with Go 1.22+:
     go install github.com/gosuda/maek/cmd/maek@latest

2. Start an agent in the background and keep it running
   (the tunnel exists only while this process is alive):

   maek agent --server __SERVER_URL__ --name my-app --target http://localhost:3000

   Flags: --name (display name) | --id (preferred id, max 32 chars)
   | --desc (short description) | --target (local URL)

3. Verify registration - poll until your service appears:

   curl __SERVER_URL__/_maek/api/services
   -> [{"id":"ab12cd","name":"my-app","connected_at":"..."}]

4. Your app is now public:

   - Browser URL: __SERVER_URL__/_maek/my-app
   - Header routing (curl/API): curl -H "X-Maek-Service: ab12cd" __SERVER_URL__/

## Notes

- No auth anywhere. Closing the agent process closes the tunnel.
- Browser URLs accept the service name or id: __SERVER_URL__/_maek/<name-or-id>
- Source: https://github.com/gosuda/maek
